final_diagnosis.text: Paroxysmal nocturnal haemoglobinuria presenting as dialysis-dependent acute kidney injury from haemoglobin cast nephropathy, with a positive DAT (IgG and C3d), intrarenal and right iliac venous thrombosis, and a falsely normal conventional CD55/CD59 flow cytometry after transfusion

secondary_findings: Positive DAT (IgG and C3d), most likely complement fragment deposition from ongoing complement activation, not autoimmune haemolytic anaemia
Right iliac vein thrombosis and intrarenal venous thrombosis
Inappropriately low reticulocyte count and falling platelets: marrow involvement
Small perirenal haematoma after the kidney biopsy
accepted_differential: Warm or mixed autoimmune haemolytic anaemia (positive DAT)
Thrombotic microangiopathy: TTP, HUS after diarrhoea, or complement-mediated (atypical) HUS
Rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis, lupus nephritis or ANCA vasculitis
Drug-induced or infection-associated haemolysis and AKI (after influenza)
Aplastic anaemia or another marrow failure syndrome
Heparin-induced thrombocytopenia (falling platelets on dialysis heparin)
key_discriminators: urine blood 2+ with few red cells
haemoglobin casts with tubular haemosiderin on biopsy
treatment_given: Emergency haemodialysis (12-16 March), four units of washed red cells, empirical methylprednisolone 40 mg/day from 19 March (stopped 21 April). Prophylactic low-molecular-weight heparin 5,000 IU daily from 23 March because of a small post-biopsy perirenal haematoma, then therapeutic rivaroxaban 15 mg twice daily from 2 April. Meningococcal vaccination at the patient's request before eculizumab, started 21 April (600 mg weekly for four weeks, then 900 mg every two weeks).
outcome: Haematological remission and progressive renal recovery: haemoglobin, LDH, creatinine and platelets returned to normal over seven months of follow-up (values only in Figure 1).

must_do.text: Dialyse urgently for oliguric AKI with uraemia and hyperkalaemia
Ask specifically about previous episodes of dark urine
Exclude a thrombotic microangiopathy: blood film for fragments and ADAMTS13 activity
Obtain a kidney biopsy to establish the cause of the AKI
Send high-sensitivity FLAER-based flow cytometry, and do not accept a normal conventional CD55/CD59 result after transfusion
Look for venous thrombosis and anticoagulate once the biopsy site allows
Vaccinate against meningococcus before starting a complement C5 inhibitor, then start it

must_not_do.text: Escalate immunosuppression for presumed autoimmune haemolysis on the DAT alone (rituximab, cytotoxics, splenectomy)
Start plasma exchange for presumed TTP with no red cell fragments and ADAMTS13 activity of 53%
Start a complement inhibitor without meningococcal vaccination
Exclude the diagnosis on a normal conventional CD55/CD59 result without a high-sensitivity test

diagnosis_rubric_anchors.5: Paroxysmal nocturnal haemoglobinuria, with the kidney injury attributed to haemolysis (haemoglobin cast nephropathy)
diagnosis_rubric_anchors.4: Paroxysmal nocturnal haemoglobinuria, without explaining the kidney injury
diagnosis_rubric_anchors.3: Haem-pigment nephropathy or tubular necrosis from intravascular haemolysis, cause not identified
diagnosis_rubric_anchors.2: Autoimmune haemolysis, a thrombotic microangiopathy (TTP, HUS or complement-mediated HUS), rhabdomyolysis or aplastic anaemia as the final diagnosis
diagnosis_rubric_anchors.1: Unrelated diagnosis, or one that would lead to harm

teaching_points: Dark urine with dipstick blood but few red cells on microscopy means haemoglobinuria or myoglobinuria; the CK separates them.
Haemolysis with a low reticulocyte count points to marrow involvement, not isolated autoimmune haemolysis.
A positive DAT (including C3d) can occur in complement-mediated haemolysis; it does not establish AIHA on its own.
Conventional CD55/CD59 flow cytometry can be falsely normal after transfusion and with limited gating; high-sensitivity FLAER-based testing on granulocytes is the standard.
Kidney biopsy with haemoglobin casts and tubular haemosiderin identifies haem-pigment injury and can redirect the work-up.
Vaccinate against meningococcus (or give antibiotic cover) before complement C5 inhibition.
